FR-C1: partly built: kernel/dispatch.py envelope() writes each builder envelope from its contract task with the goal (each served requirement's id and statement), the contract revision, the base revision, the requirement references, the write scope and the required evidence (each visible criterion with a test named by its id that must fail first; a repair round adds the gate's objections); the role and the wall time travel on the command line (`gnomon task --role builder --deadline <s>`), and the step limits are the role's max_steps and max_steps_total on the lane's surface. not built: the envelope has no read scope, no token budget, no per-envelope step budget, no stop condition and no parent, and there are no nested envelopes, so nothing inherits or narrows a limit; the write scope it names is not enforced per task either, since Gnomon enforces the surface's write_allow, compiled once per product. It would take a structured envelope that Gnomon reads from --task-file and per-run scope narrowing (upstream gaps 1 and 2 in the brief's section 10; Gnomon issue #266), then a parent field and a kernel check that a child's limits sit inside its parent's.
FR-C3: partly built: the builder and the verifier are Gnomon roles on every product lane's compiled surface (kernel/lanes.py write_product_surface); the dispatcher runs the builder per envelope in a lane leased to its task, and the gate (kernel/gate.py) runs the read-only verifier, on another model family, in the same lane; a builder's change merges only when its criterion tests fail first and the verifier has no high in-scope finding. The factory's own hand-kept surface (.gnomon/roles.toml) also defines a read-only scout, but the kernel never compiles or dispatches one. not built: no scout, assembler, repairer or triager role exists on any surface the kernel compiles. Repair rounds reuse the builder role with the objections carried, with no failure-class catalogue or sweep; seams are fixed in the spec and walked by the kernel's own holdout runner against the running service (kernel/operate.py run_holdouts; FR-E4, FR-O3), not by an assembler cell; triage and amendment drafting run on the analyst role in the toolless analyst lane (kernel/change.py) and nothing clusters signals; the verifier never sees holdouts, which the kernel runs itself. Each missing role would need its own compiled role block, a dispatch path that runs it, and a result shape the gate can judge.
FR-C4: partly built: live progress reaches the factory from the running cell's Gnomon audit trail in its leased lane (kernel/status.py live), and the cockpit (GET /api/projects/<pid>/live and the project list's running flag) and the MCP server serve it. not built: nothing in the kernel speaks Gnomon's ACP (`gnomon acp`): progress is read from the trail file on each request rather than streamed, and no Gnomon permission request reaches a person, because cells run `gnomon task --yes`, which pre-approves writes inside the role's scope, so the cockpit has no Gnomon approval to answer. It would take an ACP client in the dispatcher that relays session updates and permission asks as cockpit cards and sends the person's answer back to Gnomon before the cell continues.
